new_packages.label: עֵת רָצוֹן וּמֵצַח הָרָצוֹן
new_packages.label_en: Time of Divine Favor and the Forehead of Will

supporting_edges.quote: כְּמוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת בְּמִנְחָה, בְּחִינַת: וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּתִי... עֵת רָצוֹן

new_packages.justification: This package groups the three concepts that together constitute the single supernal moment in which the universal redemption (פִּדְיוֹן הַכּוֹלֵל) can operate. The Rebbe explicitly declares eit ratzon to be a bechina of metzach haratzon (revelation of the forehead of will) and gives Shabbat Mincha as the prime temporal instance of eit ratzon. All three nodes — eit ratzon, metzach haratzon, and Shabbat Mincha — are different expressions of the same spiritual reality: the moment/mode of maximal divine receptivity and favor. This is the enabling condition of the entire Torah's teaching. None of these concepts causes the others; they are all faces of the same supernal opening. The package is entirely in the domain of holiness (good polarity). The dominant node is עֵת רָצוֹן because it is explicitly named twice in the source text and is the pivot between the two bechina declarations.

new_packages.label: מֹשֶׁה בֵּין שְׁמָד לְרָצוֹן
new_packages.label_en: Moses — Mediator Between Destruction and Will

supporting_edges.quote: מֹשֶׁה עוֹמֵד בֵּין שְׁמָד לְרָצוֹן, כִּי מִסְפַּר מֹשֶׁה הוּא מְמֻצָּע בֵּין מִסְפַּר שְׁמָד לְמִסְפַּר רָצוֹן
מֹשֶׁה עוֹמֵד בֵּין שְׁמָד לְרָצוֹן, כִּי מִסְפַּר מֹשֶׁה הוּא מְמֻצָּע בֵּין מִסְפַּר שְׁמָד לְמִסְפַּר רָצוֹן

new_packages.justification: This package groups Moses with the two concepts whose gematria flanks his own. The Rebbe explicitly declares: 'Moses stands between shemad and ratzon, for Moses' number is the midpoint between the number of shemad and the number of ratzon.' Gematria: שְׁמָד = 344, מֹשֶׁה = 345, רָצוֹן = 346. These three are not cause-and-effect — Moses does not produce shemad or ratzon; rather, his essential identity IS the median between them. They are three aspects of the same structural reality in Moses' cosmic function. This is a rare and precise gematria-bechina: consecutive integers establishing an exact ontological midpoint. The package is polarity 'good' because it centers on Moses as the redemptive, sweetening presence. The two flanking concepts (shemad and ratzon) are within the package because the Rebbe frames them as part of Moses' essential identity-field, not as external things Moses acts upon. Note: רָצוֹן here is a companion concept to עֵת רָצוֹן in Package 1 — both reflect the same supernal reality. The full traversal of the Torah graph would connect Moses (Package 2) through ratzon to Package 1's eit ratzon, showing how Moses' death at Shabbat Mincha (Package 1) is the ultimate expression of his Package 2 identity.

new_packages.label: עַכּוּ"ם וְחֲרוֹן אַף

supporting_edges.quote: כִּי כָּל זְמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ עַכּוּ"ם בָּעוֹלָם חֲרוֹן אַף בָּעוֹלָם

new_packages.justification: This package groups the three concepts that together constitute the domain of judgment/opposition that the universal redemption addresses. The Rebbe cites a rabbinic dictum establishing the bechina equation between עַכּוּ"ם (idol worshippers) and חֲרוֹן אַף (divine wrath): their presence in the world is ontologically co-extensive — they are two faces of the same negative spiritual reality. The 24 courts of judgment (כ"ד בָּתֵּי דִּינִים) are the structural apparatus of this domain; they represent the 24 faces/dimensions of the charon af/akum complex that requires sweetening. All three nodes share the same essential nature: they are manifestations of divine distance, judgment, and opposition to holiness. This package is the evil mirror of Package 1 (charon af vs. eit ratzon/divine favor) — the entire Torah describes the movement FROM Package 3 (charon af, judgment, akum) TO Package 1 (ratzon, favor, universal sweetening) via Package 2 (Moses as the cosmic mediator). The dominant node is חֲרוֹן אַף because it appears most frequently in the teaching (lines 5, 6, 7) and is the concept most directly targeted by Moses' work.

observations:
Torah #215 requires three new packages because its bechina edges are entirely absent from the dataset. The two existing eitza edges (IDs 629 and 2095) correctly represent causal flow but cannot anchor any package — packages are built exclusively from bechina edges per the framework.

The three proposed packages correspond to the Torah's three-domain structure:
- Package 1 (good): The supernal channel — eit ratzon / metzach haratzon / Shabbat Mincha
- Package 2 (good): The human/divine agent — Moses, positioned as the exact midpoint between shemad and ratzon
- Package 3 (evil): The target domain — akum / charon af / 24 courts

The Torah's argument in three moves:
[Pkg 3: evil] →eitza→ [Pkg 1: good] →eitza→ [result: גרים]
[Pkg 2: good] mediates by acting at Pkg 1 (Moses dies at Shabbat Mincha) to transform Pkg 3.

Good/evil mirror structure (framework section 4):
- Package 1 (עֵת רָצוֹן, divine favor) directly mirrors Package 3 (חֲרוֹן אַף, divine wrath). They are the same cosmic attribute — divine will — in its two orientations: favorable and wrathful. The sweetening described in the Torah is literally the transformation of Package 3 into Package 1: charon af → ratzon.
- Package 2 (Moses, the mediator) has no evil mirror in this Torah. Moses' mediating function is entirely positive; the evil pole is Package 3 itself.

Cross-Torah connections anticipated:
- עֵת רָצוֹן appears in multiple Torahs throughout Likutay Moharan (e.g., referenced in Torahs connected to Shabbat and prayer). This node will serve as a bridge between Torah 215's Package 1 and those Torahs.
- מֹשֶׁה appears in numerous Torahs. His appearance here as the exact gematria median between shemad and ratzon is a distinctive bechina unique to Torah 215.
- חֲרוֹן אַף and גֵּרִים both appear in other Torahs (e.g., the eitza edge 629 connects to גרים discussions in Torah 17 and Torah 53). Torah 215's bechina backbone distinguishes it: it explains WHY the sweetening produces converts (because akum = charon af in the first place).
